nnnTemplate:
CUSTOM+ — NNN AGREEMENT TEMPLATE
(Non disclosure, Non use, Non circumvention)

This is a starting template, not legal advice. Have it reviewed by a
lawyer qualified in Chinese contract law before using it with a real
factory.

WHY AN NNN AND NOT JUST AN NDA
A standard Western NDA is built to stop one thing: someone talking
about your product. It is commonly difficult to enforce in Chinese
courts and does nothing about the two risks that actually matter in
manufacturing — a factory using your design for itself, or going
around you to sell directly to your customers or retailers. An NNN,
drafted for Chinese jurisdiction, covers all three.

1. NON DISCLOSURE
   The Receiving Party will not disclose the Disclosing Party's
   technical drawings, specifications, tooling data, or business
   information to any third party without prior written consent.
   > Plain language: stops them from talking about your product to
   people who have no reason to know about it.

2. NON USE
   The Receiving Party will not use the disclosed information for any
   purpose other than manufacturing the Disclosing Party's product
   under this agreement — including not using it to develop,
   manufacture, or sell a similar product for itself or any other
   party.
   > Plain language: stops the factory from quietly making and
   selling your product themselves.

3. NON CIRCUMVENTION
   The Receiving Party will not contact the Disclosing Party's
   customers, distributors, or retailers directly, or otherwise
   bypass the Disclosing Party, using relationships or information
   gained through this engagement.
   > Plain language: stops the factory from going around you to sell
   straight to the people you sell to.

4. GOVERNING LAW & JURISDICTION
   This agreement is governed by the laws of the People's Republic
   of China, with disputes subject to the jurisdiction of [City]
   courts or [CIETAC / other named arbitration body]. The Chinese
   language version controls in case of translation conflict.

5. TERM
   This agreement remains in effect for [X years] from the date of
   signature, regardless of whether a manufacturing relationship
   results.

6. PENALTY CLAUSE
   A specific liquidated damages figure, stated in RMB, is what
   actually gives an NNN teeth in Chinese courts — a vague
   "damages as determined" clause is far harder to enforce than a
   stated number.

PARTIES
Disclosing Party: _______________________
Receiving Party (Factory): _______________________
Signed: _______________________   Date: _______________________

review before signing with a real factory.
aqlChecklist:
CUSTOM+ — AQL PRE SHIPMENT INSPECTION CHECKLIST

Used before releasing final payment on any production run.

1. SAMPLING
   [ ] Inspection level confirmed (General Level II is standard for
       most consumer goods; Special Levels for destructive or costly
       tests)
   [ ] Sample size drawn per ANSI/ASQ Z1.4 tables against total batch
       size
   [ ] Samples drawn randomly across pallets/cartons, not hand picked

2. AQL THRESHOLDS (confirm before production starts, not at
   inspection)
   [ ] Critical defects — AQL 0 (zero tolerance)
   [ ] Major defects — AQL 2.5 (typical)
   [ ] Minor defects — AQL 4.0 (typical)

3. WHAT GETS CHECKED
   [ ] Visual — cosmetic defects, color match, surface finish
   [ ] Dimensional — measured against the approved golden sample
   [ ] Function — the product actually does what it's supposed to
   [ ] Packaging — carton strength, labeling, barcode scan test
   [ ] Safety/compliance markings present and correct

4. TIMING (don't rely on pre shipment alone)
   [ ] IQC — incoming materials checked before production starts
   [ ] IPQC — in process checks during the run, not just at the end
   [ ] FQC / pre shipment — final check before the batch ships

5. DOCUMENTATION
   [ ] Defect counts logged by category (critical/major/minor)
   [ ] Pass/fail line stated against the agreed AQL threshold
   [ ] Photos attached for any defects found
   [ ] Inspector name and signature on the report
   [ ] Report dated and tied to a specific batch/PO number

6. IF IT FAILS
   [ ] Rework or reject terms confirmed in writing before this
       moment, not negotiated after the fact
   [ ] Who bears the cost of rework/reshipment stated in the contract

— Provided by CUSTOM+.
dfmChecklist:
CUSTOM+ — DFM (DESIGN FOR MANUFACTURABILITY) REVIEW CHECKLIST

Run before a design is called "manufacturable" and before tooling is
quoted.

1. WALL THICKNESS
   [ ] Consistent wall thickness throughout the part (avoids sink
       marks, warping, uneven cooling)
   [ ] Thickness matches the chosen material and process (injection
       molding tolerances differ from CNC or sheet metal)

2. DRAFT ANGLES
   [ ] Every vertical surface has draft (typically 1–2 degrees
       minimum) so the part actually releases from the mold
   [ ] Textured surfaces have extra draft — texture adds friction

3. UNDERCUTS
   [ ] Undercuts identified and resolved (side action tooling,
       redesign, or accepted as a cost/complexity tradeoff — not
       discovered after tooling is cut)

4. TOLERANCE STACK UP
   [ ] Critical dimensions identified and tolerance requirements set
       deliberately, not defaulted
   [ ] Stack up checked across mating parts, not each part in
       isolation

5. GATE & PARTING LINE PLACEMENT
   [ ] Gate location won't leave a visible mark on a cosmetic
       surface
   [ ] Parting line placement reviewed for both function and
       appearance

6. MATERIAL SELECTION
   [ ] Material matches the actual use case (UV exposure, flex
       fatigue, chemical exposure, food contact, temperature range)
   [ ] Material available at the target factory, not a specialty
       grade that adds lead time

7. ASSEMBLY METHOD
   [ ] Fastening method reviewed (snap fit, screw, ultrasonic weld,
       adhesive) for both cost and field serviceability
   [ ] Assembly sequence makes sense on a real production line, not
       just on paper

8. COMPLIANCE FLAGS
   [ ] Target market certifications identified early (CE, FCC, RoHS,
       etc.) — these can constrain material and design choices
   [ ] Compliance testing timeline built into the schedule, not added
       after tooling

— Provided by CUSTOM+.
